note: Allow site to be iframed removes the X-Frame-Options response header on selected paths so those pages can be embedded in an <iframe>. A response event subscriber (RemoveXFrameOptionsSubscriber, priority -10 on KernelEvents::RESPONSE) evaluates core's request_path condition and removes the header on matching responses. Configuration lives in allow_iframed_site.settings under the request_path key: pages (newline path list) and negate (0/1). The settings form is /admin/config/system/allow_iframed_site (permission administer site configuration); saving it flushes all caches. If pages is empty and negate is 0 the header is kept (no-op). The module ships no config/install and no config schema - the config is created on first save. It manages only X-Frame-Options, not CSP frame-ancestors. Medium cases read the live request_path config; hard cases set it (allow a path; negate to allow-everywhere-except), verified live. Baseline is restored by deleting allow_iframed_site.settings.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal allow_iframed_site module do to let a page be embedded in an iframe? Name the specific HTTP response header involved.
evals.expected_output: It removes the X-Frame-Options response header on the paths you select (via a response event subscriber), so those pages are no longer blocked from being framed by other origins.

evals.prompt: Using allow_iframed_site, how do I choose which paths are allowed to be iframed, and where is that stored?
evals.expected_output: On the settings form at /admin/config/system/allow_iframed_site (permission 'administer site configuration') you enter paths using core's Request path condition (a Pages list plus a Negate toggle). It is stored in allow_iframed_site.settings under the request_path key (pages + negate).

evals.prompt: What is the security risk of using allow_iframed_site to remove X-Frame-Options, and what does the negate option do?
evals.expected_output: Removing X-Frame-Options re-exposes those pages to clickjacking (the module warns 'Watch out for clickjacking!'), so scope the paths tightly. The Negate option inverts the match: with negate on, the header is stripped everywhere EXCEPT the listed pages.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, allow_iframed_site is configured so that certain paths can be embedded in an iframe. Inspect the live configuration and list the path(s) that are allowed to be framed.
evals.expected_output: The framable paths are /aisframe-demo and /aisframe-demo/*: allow_iframed_site.settings.request_path.pages = "/aisframe-demo\n/aisframe-demo/*" with negate off.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the allow_iframed_site configuration. Is framing allowed only on the listed path, or everywhere except it? Explain what the current request_path setting means.
evals.expected_output: Negate is on: allow_iframed_site.settings.request_path has negate = true and pages = /np-except, so X-Frame-Options is removed (framing allowed) everywhere EXCEPT /np-except.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the allow_iframed_site module to allow the path /embed-ok to be embedded in an iframe (remove X-Frame-Options for that path only, without negating). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set allow_iframed_site.settings.request_path.pages to include /embed-ok with negate off (via the Request path condition on /admin/config/system/allow_iframed_site, or by saving the request_path config). The response subscriber then removes X-Frame-Options on /embed-ok.

evals.prompt: I want my site's pages to be embeddable in iframes everywhere, except I do NOT want the /admin area to be framable. Using the 'Allow site to be iframed' module, set that up and make it live.
evals.expected_output: Configure allow_iframed_site.settings.request_path with pages listing /admin and negate = true, so X-Frame-Options is removed everywhere except /admin (set via the Pages list + Negate checkbox on the settings form, or by saving the request_path config).
